title: Tokyo cash shut, Osaka open — the Rule 3(3) in-between day, and the night session that is live when the US 2-Year auction prints
source: EST: jpx.co.jp/english/corporate/about-jpx/calendar/index.html (Market Holidays, page's own 'Update : Feb. 06, 2026'), re-fetched direct 2026-09-15 (HTTP 200, 33,103 bytes) — the 2026 panel reads verbatim 'Sep. 22 (Tue.) Holiday 2', and footnote 2 reads verbatim 'September 22, 2026, is a holiday in accordance with Rule 3, Paragraph 3 of Act on National Holidays' (the weekday-between-two-holidays rule; 09-21 Respect for the Aged Day, 09-23 Autumnal Equinox). Corroborated at three further primaries in the same session: jpx.co.jp/english/derivatives/rules/holidaytrading/index.html (HTTP 200, 48,483 bytes, 'Update : Jun. 26, 2026'), whose eligible-holiday table carries 'September 22 | Tue. | Holiday 5 | Open | Finalized'; the exchange's List_of_Finalized_Holiday_Trading_Days_E.xlsx (HTTP 200, 11,884 bytes, 77 entries 2022-09-23 -> 2027-05-05), parsed cell by cell, which carries Excel serial 46287 = 2026-09-22, Name 'Holiday', Markets 'Open'; and Japan's Cabinet Office national-holiday file www8.cao.go.jp/chosei/shukujitsu/syukujitsu.csv (HTTP 200, 21,538 bytes, Shift-JIS, 1,067 holidays 1955-01-01 -> 2027-11-23), whose 2026 rows read 2026/9/21 Respect for the Aged Day, 2026/9/22 'holiday', 2026/9/23 Autumnal Equinox. Stays estimate on the two standing counts the sibling jpx-market-closure entries record, neither of them date doubt: market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a securities exchange's own holiday calendar, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-15
notes: Canonical file written by this event's own initial research (2026-09-15, D-7) after reading the sole proposal, .from-treasury-2y-note-2026-09-22, which is now shadowed. WHAT IS ACTUALLY SHUT: the Tokyo CASH equity market only. JPX carries 2026-09-21, 09-22 and 09-23 all as 'Open | Finalized' for derivatives holiday trading on two independent primaries, so index futures, index options, commodity futures and options on commodity futures run an 08:45-15:45 JST day session AND a 17:00-06:00 night session on each of the three days. The proposal's 'Tokyo dark for five consecutive sessions' framing is therefore false for derivatives and was corrected first by the 09-21 sibling ledger; this entry's own contribution is what the 09-22 night session means for the corridor. THE TIMING FACT SPECIFIC TO THIS DATE: the 2-Year note auction (treasury-2y-note-2026-09-22, confirmed, 1:00pm ET per Treasury's tentative auction schedule) prices at 02:00 JST on 09-23 — inside the 09-22 holiday NIGHT session. So a Japanese equity-index hedge is continuously available across the auction print while JGB futures, options on JGB futures, interest-rate futures and securities options are ineligible for holiday trading and dark all three days. THE PUBLICATION FACT, NEW THIS SESSION: JPX publishes no separate daily report for a holiday-trading session — its own trading-day rule folds 09-21/22/23 into the trading day that ends with the 09-24 day session, and the daily-report index for May 2026 confirms it (no 20260504/05/06 entries; volume lands on 20260507). So per-session holiday volume is not obtainable from JPX daily statistics at all, which answers rather than fills the 09-21 sibling's open item. THE MEASURED NULL, THIS SESSION'S OWN WORK: whether OSE traded through a cash closure or was shut alongside it makes no difference to where the first cash bar's move happens. On the exchange's own Open/Not Open labels, the first ^N225 session back runs mean |overnight gap| 0.748% (n=39, traded through) vs 0.769% (n=8, shut), Welch t=-0.110, and mean |intraday| 0.853% vs 0.769%, t=+0.292; difference-in-differences against the pre-launch era netting out ordinary sessions gives -0.078pp on the gap (t=-0.831) and +0.049pp intraday (t=+0.333) — the wrong sign for any 'futures priced it through so the cash opens at fair value' story. The relocation signature (|gap| >= 2x|intraday|) fires on 31% of traded-through sessions, 34% of pre-launch ones and 28% of ordinary sessions: the same rate either way. Impact low: no Japan-listed symbol is tracked here and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates- or Tokyo-keyed. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
